body.normal: FC-GPR is the report an Indian company files with the Reserve Bank of India after it issues shares to a foreign investor. It is filed on the RBI's FIRMS portal within 30 days of issuing the shares.
body.simple: FC-GPR tells the Reserve Bank of India that a foreign company bought shares in your Indian company.
body.detail: Under FEMA, foreign investment into an Indian company must be reported to the RBI. When the company issues shares to a person resident outside India, it files Form FC-GPR through the FIRMS portal within 30 days of the allotment. The filing includes the foreign inward remittance details, the bank's KYC report on the investor, a valuation certificate and a declaration from the company secretary. Late filing attracts a late submission fee.
body.why: Your parent company's share money is foreign investment, so this report keeps the investment on record with the RBI and avoids penalties.
